principles.name: Determinize stable decisions
principles.mechanism: Move a well-specified repeated decision into a reproducible tool or check, leaving interpretation to the agent.
principles.applicability: Inputs, expected behavior and failure conditions are stable enough to specify and test.
principles.tradeoffs: A premature rule can freeze a wrong assumption. Include maintenance and exception handling in its cost.
principles.triz_connection: Transfer functions to an existing subsystem; preliminary action; removal of repeated reasoning.

principles.name: Apply complexity conditionally
principles.mechanism: Invoke an expensive review, model or mechanism only when a measured condition justifies it.
principles.applicability: There is a useful low-cost routing signal and a bounded consequence for a missed trigger.
principles.tradeoffs: Detection can miss difficult cases or become more expensive than the work it saves.
principles.triz_connection: Separation by condition; local quality; dynamic adjustment.

principles.name: Verify independently
principles.mechanism: Check a result against an independently controlled acceptance artifact or executor.
principles.applicability: A testable external acceptance condition exists or can be defined before the change.
principles.tradeoffs: Verification costs resources and may share blind spots with implementation. A second opinion is not automatically independent evidence.
principles.triz_connection: Separation between system roles; feedback; intermediary.

principles.name: Revise falsified hypotheses
principles.mechanism: When repeated evidence contradicts the working explanation, select a discriminating test and update the explanation before retrying.
principles.applicability: Repeated failures have comparable inputs and a new test can distinguish plausible causes.
principles.tradeoffs: Changing strategy too quickly can abandon valid recovery from a transient condition.
principles.triz_connection: Cause-effect analysis; overcoming fixation; separation by observed condition.

principles.name: Refresh context with evidence
principles.mechanism: Give a fresh reasoning pass a compact factual state, source links and the unresolved question.
principles.applicability: Long context contains stale assumptions or contradictory plans and the relevant facts can be preserved.
principles.tradeoffs: Summaries can omit constraints. Context refresh must preserve the task, authority and unresolved evidence.
principles.triz_connection: Separation in time and between roles; removal of harmful accumulated state.

principles.name: Remove the source of harm
principles.mechanism: Repair or remove the faulty function at its owner instead of repeatedly compensating for its symptoms.
principles.applicability: The causal source is sufficiently established and the owning component can be changed within the task mandate.
principles.tradeoffs: A broad root-cause intervention can exceed the needed scope. Verify dependencies and the effect of removal.
principles.triz_connection: Function analysis; trimming; elimination of harmful interactions.

principles.name: Learn from measured outcomes
principles.mechanism: Turn observations into scoped hypotheses, compare interventions and retain positive as well as negative outcomes.
principles.applicability: Future tasks have enough relevant similarity for a bounded comparison and reuse.
principles.tradeoffs: Analysis, retrieval and stale rules can cost more than they save. Prevent leakage between discovery and evaluation.
principles.triz_connection: Feedback; self-service; reuse of existing informational resources.

principles.name: Make interventions reversible
principles.mechanism: Version the changed artifact and define a tested path to restore the previous state or disable the intervention.
principles.applicability: The effect can be isolated or compensated for, and the restoration condition is explicit.
principles.tradeoffs: A source-code rollback may not undo external writes or migrated data. Reversibility must be tested at the affected boundary.
principles.triz_connection: Separation in time; temporary action; recovery after useful action.

principles.name: Control on meaningful deviation
principles.mechanism: Intervene when progress, outcomes or constraints deviate from a declared expectation rather than supervising every action.
principles.applicability: There is an observable progress or outcome signal and an appropriate intervention budget.
principles.tradeoffs: Poor progress proxies can reward busywork or misclassify legitimate waiting. Thresholds need contextual calibration.
principles.triz_connection: Feedback; separation by condition; economical use of supervisory resources.

principles.name: Place the function at the sufficient level
principles.mechanism: Move a function to the smallest existing layer that can perform it correctly, removing redundant higher-level work.
principles.applicability: An existing tool, interface, test or configuration already owns the relevant state or invariant.
principles.tradeoffs: A lower layer may lack intent or context. Preserve a clear contract and avoid hidden global behavior.
principles.triz_connection: Separation between system levels; redistribution of functions; trimming.

principles.name: Route using scoped evidence
principles.mechanism: Select the model, tool or strategy using relevant measured outcomes and the current task constraints.
principles.applicability: Alternatives exist, their interfaces are compatible and evidence is scoped to the present environment.
principles.tradeoffs: A router adds overhead and can overfit stale or sparse data. Keep a transparent fallback and report uncertainty.
principles.triz_connection: Separation by condition; local quality; dynamic resource assignment.

principles.name: Ground completion in acceptance evidence
principles.mechanism: Determine completion from the agreed deliverables and observed acceptance results.
principles.applicability: The requested outcome can be associated with checkable artifacts or explicit external acceptance.
principles.tradeoffs: Overly elaborate gates can delay simple work. A fixed gate can miss a changed user goal and must retain the original scope.
principles.triz_connection: Feedback; elimination of redundant status inference; alignment of the useful function with its outcome.
